subject: Primary/Secondary Region Eligibility + Burst Guardrails for Dedicated Pool
messages:
From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@luminahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@luminahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool — primary/secondary regions + surge constraints

Hi Tessa / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move into Dedicated capacity and want to align on regional selection and burst rules before the SOW is finalized. High-level asks from my side:

- We need a primary region for lowest-latency traffic (US-WEST) and a secondary region for failover and scheduled bursting.
- Peak QPS expectation: ~120 rps at inference time (95th percentile); average ~35 rps.
- Compliance: all inference must remain within US-based regions for now.
- Procurement asks for an explicit burst policy (how long, how often, cost impact) to include in the contract.

I've attached our traffic sample and SLOs. Can you propose a straightforward primary/secondary eligibility approach and a guardrail-based burst policy we can present to procurement?

Appreciate it — looking to lock the SOW next week.

Best,
Rajesh
Director, Platform Engineering
LuminaHealth
[Attachment: lumina_traffic_sample.csv (CSV)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool — primary/secondary regions + surge constraints

Rajesh — thanks for the context and the sample. I'm attaching a lightweight worksheet that maps requirements to two feasible topologies. Summary up front:

1) Option A — Single primary (us-west-2) + warm secondary (us-east-1)
   - Pros: lowest average latency for west-coast traffic; fast failover to east; modest cross-region traffic only during failover or short bursts.
   - Autoscale/burst model: steady pool sized for baseline (40 GPU tokens equivalent) + burst window that can add up to +50% capacity for 30 minutes, up to 6x per month.

2) Option B — Dual-active (us-west-2 + us-east-1, traffic steering by latency)
   - Pros: more headroom, lower failover RTO; better support for geo-distributed clients.
   - Cons: higher standing cost. Burst policy can be more permissive (75% extra) since both regions supply capacity.

Action items I propose:
- Ben to validate GPU sizing assumptions with an initial workload simulation.
- Monica to prepare the operational runbook (on-call routing, fallback play).
- We provide procurement with a short appendix describing burst frequency/cost tradeoffs for each option.

I've attached: lumina_capacity_workbook.xlsx (estimates) and a preview SOW v0.3. Ben — any initial feedback on the proposed burst ceilings?

Thanks,
Tessa
Senior CS Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: lumina_capacity_workbook.xlsx (XLSX)]

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool — primary/secondary regions + surge constraints

Folks — quick technical read: I ran the traffic sample through our estimator and used Redwood quantization profiles for the model you mentioned in the demo (gpt-medium-8b-equivalent pipeline). Highlights:

- Baseline sizing: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs in us-west-2 will cover ~35 rps sustained with room for KV cache and batching headroom.
- Burst sizing: to hit 120 rps (95th) with similar latency targets we estimate ~28 GPU-equivalents momentarily. That implies burst capacity of +130% on top of baseline.
- Warm secondary: keeping a hot/standby mini-pool of 4 GPUs in us-east-1 gives a sub-90s failover for in-flight requests if we pre-warm KV caches.

Suggested guardrails (practical & procurement-friendly):
- Short bursts: up to +150% for a single contiguous 30-minute window, allowed up to 4x per month.
- Emergency bursts: up to +300% for a single 10-minute window with manual ops approval (costly).
- Auto-throttle: if average token latency crosses 450ms for more than 2 minutes, newly queued bursts will be rejected and requests routed to secondary region if eligible.

I'll add these into the appendix for the SOW and include an ops SOP for manual approval flow. Monica — I'll ping you the pre-warm KV script and an autoscale policy example.

-Ben
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: region-eligibility-matrix.csv (CSV)]

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool — primary/secondary regions + surge constraints

Rajesh — looping in a skeleton operational runbook so procurement and your ops team can see how we handle failover and burst approvals. Key items included:

- On-call flow: Redwood Ops triage -> if impact > P2, escalate to L2 and notify Lumina on-call within 5min.
- Pre-warm window: 10 minutes before scheduled burst (via API call or webhook).
- Cost-visibility: token- and GPU-level accounting per region; daily emailed cost reports during first 30 days.

Open question for Lumina: do you want automated scheduled bursts (e.g., nightly batch windows) or manual-trigger-only for each event? Scheduled bursts let us pre-warm and reduce latency, manual-trigger reduces accidental spend.

Monica
Customer Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — procurement reviewed the appendix and had these asks:

1) Move the default allowed burst frequency to 3x/month (from 4x) and include per-burst cost cap.
2) Require that emergency bursts (up to +300%) require a named approver from Lumina and a secondary approver from Redwood (we'll provide a short list).
3) Please add a short paragraph in the SOW clarifying that all data paths for model inference will remain in US regions and not cross into EU or APAC.

We prefer scheduled bursts for nightly ETL windows (we do 2 nightly jobs), but want manual approval for ad-hoc spikes. Can you add a simple API-trigger sample we can call from our scheduler?

Will review updated SOW once you send.

Thanks,
Elena
